feedback.problem: Given $X∼\text{Geom}(0.3),$ compute $P(X>5)$ rounded to $4$ decimal places.
feedback.worked_solution:
If $X∼\text{Geom}(p),$ then $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}(1-p)^{x-1}p, & x=1,2,3,… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Here, $X∼\text{Geom}(0.3),$ so the distribution of $X$ in this case is

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}(0.7)^{x-1}(0.3), & x=1,2,3… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

There are infinitely many values of $X$ such that $X>5.$ However, we can simplify the computation by using the complement instead:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>5) & =1-P(X\le 5)\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the complement, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 5) & =P(X\in {1,2,3,4,5}) \\  & =P(X=1)+P(X=2)+P(X=3)+P(X=4)+P(X=5) \\  & =f(1)+f(2)+f(3)+f(4)+f(5) \\  & =(0.7)^{0}(0.3)+(0.7)^{1}(0.3)+(0.7)^{2}(0.3)+(0.7)^{3}(0.3)+(0.7)^{4}(0.3) \\  & ≈0.8319.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>5) & =1-P(X\le 5) \\  & ≈1-0.8319 \\  & =0.1681.\end{aligned}
$$
